title: Now May He Who from the Dead
description: Now May He Who from the Dead in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 100, “Heb 13:20,24”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now may He who from the dead Brought the Shep-herd of the sheep, Je-sus Christ, our King and Head, All our souls in safe-ty keep!

lines: Now may He who from the dead
Brought the Shepherd of the sheep,
Jesus Christ, our King and Head,
All our souls in safety keep!
May he teach us to fulfill
What is pleasing in his sight;
Perfect us in all his will,
And preserve us day and night!
Who the cov'nant sealed with blood,
Let our hearts and voices raise

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
